analysis:
This PR changes only documentation: a new changelog fragment (changelog.d/qwen38-reasoning-effort-400.md) and additions to docs/architecture/inference.md (new paragraph near head line 1118 and a failure-table row near line 1517). No source code is in the supplied batch. The docs describe a behavior change: unsupported reasoning efforts on Qwen3.8-27B (as on Flash-Next) are rejected with a typed HTTP 400 before Jinja rendering. Typed request errors from media preparation are rethrown rather than wrapped as a retryable 503 capacity_busy.

Security-relevant reading: this moves caller-controlled input validation ahead of template rendering, which reduces misclassification of client faults as provider faults (500/503). It does not touch encryption, attestation, authorization, the prefix cache (T-041), or the coordinator/provider boundary (TB-002, T-008). The error messages are described as typed client errors. The docs do not say whether error detail echoes caller input. The actual change in Qwen4SupportPolicy.swift (`validateReasoningContext`) and in the media-preparation rethrow path is NOT in the supplied evidence, so I cannot confirm these claims.

Open questions for deeper review of the code: (1) whether the rethrow of typed errors in vision preparation still releases media/memory charges and service leases on that path, to avoid resource leaks or charging gaps; (2) whether the 400 error body avoids leaking prompt content (A-001) through sanitizedInferenceFailure; (3) whether the 400 vs 503 reclassification affects coordinator retry or billing behavior, since a non-retryable client error should not be billed or rerouted. These cannot be settled from docs alone. The 9bceb6d953b336e2:3 base text unit was reviewed and is unchanged context. No findings are raised.
